test_cases.test_name: End-to-End Workflow Template Configuration and Execution
test_cases.objective: Verify that the platform can be configured with a complete patient therapy workflow template and successfully execute it, enforcing chain-of-identity and custody.
prerequisites: System installation is complete
Admin user credentials are available
Test workflow template definition document is prepared

test_steps.action: Log into the system as an administrator and navigate to the workflow configuration module.
test_steps.expected_result: Administrator successfully authenticates and gains access to the workflow configuration interface.

test_steps.action: Create a new workflow template by configuring the sequential steps for apheresis, manufacturing slot allocation, QC release, and infusion.
test_steps.expected_result: System saves the new workflow template with all configured steps and transitions without errors.

test_steps.action: Initiate a test patient journey using the newly created template and simulate a dual-scanning event at a handoff point.
test_steps.expected_result: Patient journey is initiated successfully, and the system enforces dual-scanning verification before allowing the handoff to proceed.
data_to_capture: User IDs of personnel performing scans
Audit trail entries for the handoff

acceptance_criteria: Workflow template is created and saved without errors
Patient journey progresses through all configured steps in the correct sequence
Dual-scanning verification is mandatory and successfully captured in the audit trail
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures
GDP guidelines for chain-of-custody documentation
data_integrity_requirements: All configuration changes must be recorded in the audit trail
All chain-of-identity and custody events must be immutable and time-stamped
related_tests: OQ-003 (Future test for exception handling)

test_cases.test_name: Configurable Risk Scoring and Algorithm Module Integration
test_cases.objective: Validate the configuration of risk scoring rules using vendor scripting and the integration of an optional, containerized custom algorithm module for patient matching.
prerequisites: OQ-001 is passed
A test containerized algorithm module is available
Vendor scripting guide is available

test_steps.action: Access the risk rule configuration interface and create a new scoring rule using the vendor-supplied scripting language to calculate a risk score based on patient age and product viability time.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the script, compiles it without errors, and activates the new risk scoring rule.

test_steps.action: Upload and deploy a test version of a containerized custom algorithm module for patient-to-lot matching via the designated module management interface.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the container image, deploys it successfully, and reports the module status as 'Active'.
data_to_capture: Container status from the orchestration platform

test_steps.action: Execute the risk scoring rule and the custom matching algorithm for a simulated patient case and verify the output and explainability artifact.
test_steps.expected_result: A risk score is calculated, a patient-lot match is proposed, and a log or report is generated explaining the algorithm's decision factors.

acceptance_criteria: Risk scoring rules can be configured and executed successfully using vendor scripting
Custom algorithm modules can be deployed and integrated without system errors
Algorithm decisions are accompanied by an explainability artifact
regulatory_basis: Principles of ALCOA+ for data integrity of algorithm inputs and outputs
General validation principles for automated processes
data_integrity_requirements: All script and module changes must be version-controlled
Inputs and outputs for algorithmic decisions must be logged immutably
related_tests: OQ-007 (Future test for performance under load)

test_steps.action: Initiate a patient therapy workflow and progress to first handoff point

test_steps.action: Attempt to scan incorrect material identifier during handoff
test_steps.expected_result: System rejects the scan and prevents workflow progression with appropriate error message

test_steps.action: Perform correct dual-scanning with valid material and personnel credentials
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts verification and records complete custody transfer event in audit trail

test_steps.action: Repeat verification process for multiple handoff points throughout workflow
test_steps.expected_result: System consistently enforces dual-scanning requirement at each custody transfer point

Invalid scans are rejected with appropriate error messaging
Complete audit trail records are created for all verification events

GDP Guidelines for cold chain management
FDA guidance on chain-of-identity for cell and gene therapies
data_integrity_requirements: Immutable audit trail for all scanning events
Timestamped records with user identification
Complete chain-of-custody documentation

test_steps.expected_result: System successfully allocates the slot and updates the manufacturing schedule.

test_cases.test_name: Audit Trail and E-Signature Verification for Critical Actions
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system maintains a complete and immutable audit trail for all critical actions and enforces 21 CFR Part 11 compliant e-signatures.
prerequisites: System is installed and configured
Test users with appropriate roles and permissions are created

test_steps.action: Log in as a qualified user and initiate a critical action (e.g., approve a manufacturing slot, confirm chain-of-custody handoff).
test_steps.expected_result: System prompts for an e-signature with username and password confirmation before proceeding.

test_steps.action: Enter valid credentials to apply the e-signature and complete the action.
test_steps.expected_result: Action is completed successfully, and a permanent record is created in the audit trail.

test_steps.action: Access the system's audit trail reporting feature and query for the recorded action.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail displays the complete record including user ID, timestamp, action, reason for change (if applicable), and the e-signature event.
data_to_capture: Verification that all required data fields are present and immutable

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify or delete the audit trail entry via the application interface.
test_steps.expected_result: System prevents any modification or deletion of audit trail records, demonstrating immutability.

Audit trail reports are readily available and searchable.

EU GMP Annex 11 - Clause 9 Audit Trails
data_integrity_requirements: ALCOA+ principles must be maintained for all audit trail data.
Audit trail must be immutable and time-stamped to a trusted source.
E-signatures must be legally binding and equivalent to handwritten signatures.
urs_requirements: URS-028-008: Full audit trail for all handoffs and custody events.
URS-028-009: 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures for critical actions.

test_cases.test_name: Single Sign-On (SSO) and Device Identity Integration

test_steps.expected_result: User is automatically redirected to the corporate OIDC identity provider's login page.

test_steps.action: Enter valid credentials for a test user on the identity provider's login page.
test_steps.expected_result: Authentication is successful, and the user is redirected back to the platform's main dashboard without being prompted for credentials again.

test_steps.action: Log out of the platform and close the browser. Reopen the browser and navigate to the platform URL.
test_steps.expected_result: If the identity provider session is still active, user is logged in automatically; if not, user is prompted to log in again by the identity provider.
data_to_capture: Behavior based on IdP session state
